Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: Left elbow swelling noticed about 1 week ago. Not painful, overall well. Swelling is slightly warm and feels somewhat fluid. No known injury or trauma. Able to move elbow normally.
- History of presenting illness: Swelling started about a week ago; no prior similar episodes; no systemic symptoms reported.
- Past medical history: Osteoarthritis diagnosed by GP a few years ago.
- Allergies: Peanut allergy.
- Medications: None regularly.
- Social history: Desk-based job; exercises (runs 2–3 times per week); generally healthy.
- Family history: No confirmed rheumatologic diseases reported.

Objective:
- Exam findings:
  - Left elbow with visible swelling.
  - Local warmth over the swelling.
  - Skin at the tip of the elbow appears dry.
  - Movement of the elbow normal; no significant tenderness on nerve palpation; tenderness localized near swelling described as mild.
  - No signs of septic arthritis observed on exam (elbow not acutely red or severely tender).
- Investigations:
  - Blood tests planned: inflammatory markers, infection screen, rheumatologic antibodies, and gout screening.
  - Blood test forms to be sent to patient’s home with instructions.
  - Expected turnaround: results in about 5–6 days.

Assessment & Plan:
1. Left elbow swelling with suspected bursitis (bursitis around the elbow)
   - Diagnosis/assessment: Suspected bursitis.
   - Differential diagnoses: septic arthritis (emergency to rule out if symptoms worsen), gout, inflammatory arthritis, osteoarthritis-related effusion.
   - Investigations planned: blood tests as listed above (inflammatory markers, infection screen, rheumatologic antibodies, gout).
   - Treatment planned: Ibuprofen 400 mg taken orally twice daily after meals; if heartburn occurs, discontinue.
   - Referrals/follow-up: Follow-up appointment to review after blood test results (in-person or via phone/video; arrangement discussed). If symptoms worsen (increased redness, severe pain, spreading redness), seek urgent assessment.

Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Vital signs (BP, HR, temperature) not documented.
  - No baseline imaging (e.g., X-ray or ultrasound) performed or ordered.
  - Medication reconciliation not documented beyond current plan; no other current meds listed.
- Internal conflicts: None identified; transcript consistently supports a non-septic elbow swelling with bursitis suspected.
- Transcript quality: Clear overall; minor conversational fillers present but information is coherent.
